newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC announces $1 billion China chip venture.
newsitem.headline: NEC announces $1 billion China chip venture.

text.p: Japan's biggest semiconductor maker NEC Corp formally signed an agreement with a Chinese partner on Wednesday to set up a major chip manufacturing plant in Shanghai.
An NEC spokesman said the total cost of the joint venture, the latest sign of moves by Japanese electronic makers to move into the vast China market, would be $1 billion.
He said NEC and its Chinese partner, Shanghai Hua Hong, would design, manufacture and market semiconductors using NEC's latest chip technology.
NEC would contribute 28.6 percent of the venture's $700 million capital and Shanghai Hua Hong the remaining 71.4 percent. The plant would be based in Shanghai's Pudong district.
It would start full-scale production of dynamic random access memory chips (DRAM) and applied specific integrated circuits in the first half of 1999, he said.

The plant is expected to produce about 20,000 units of the 8-inch wafers a month, to be supplied primarily to the Chinese market which is on a drive to modernise the country's information infrastructure and technology.
The spokesman said the agreement was a result of NEC's participation in China's five-year plan to develop its semiconductor industry.
It is the second big NEC investment in China following the setting up of a personal computers (PC) manufacturing plant, also in Shanghai, two years ago.
Masahiro Ono, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Securities Japan, said the new plant was a gamble on China's manufacturing and technology future.
"It's a bit risky. It's hard to predict how far NEC could raise the production yields at the new China plant," Ono said.
"It is an investment in the future."
Ono added that the plant was also part of NEC's strategy to improve cost competitiveness by shifting production lines abroad.
In 1996, global overcapacity and a slowdown in international PC sales caused a protracted freefall in DRAM prices, squeezing Japanese electronics makers, which depend heavily on DRAM production.
But production cuts by South Korean chipmakers halted the price slide early this year and helped to bolster the market, although a substantial recovery has yet to take hold.
NEC has weathered the chip storm better than other Japanese makers thanks to its strategy of pushing manufacturing abroad.
Last week the company announced a strong rise in annual profits despite the slump in chip prices, mainly on the back of Japan's booming market for mobile phones and communications gadgets.
Its group net profit rose 18 percent in the fiscal year to March 31 to 91.58 billion yen ($789 million), and it predicted earnings would edge up in the current business year.
Analysts forecast that NEC would be alone among the Japan's major chip firms in turning a profit in semiconductor operations in the 1996/97 business year.
NEC expects its semiconductor output in the current business year to March 31, 1998, to rise by 18 percent year-on-year to 1.3 trillion yen ($11.2 billion).
